attack_indicators: presence of root_shell=1 and num_root>0 indicating privilege escalation attempts
hot indicators > 0 signaling suspicious activity like system file access or program creation
high rerror_rate and srv_rerror_rate values (close to 1.0) indicating rejected connections or failed login attempts
flags such as RSTO and S3 associated with connection resets and suspicious session teardowns
low src_bytes with very high dst_bytes in some R2L attacks (e.g., warezmaster) indicating data exfiltration
logged_in=0 combined with num_failed_logins>0 indicating brute force or guessing attempts
attack_signatures: Signature 1: R2L attacks often have flag=RSTO or SF with high rerror_rate (≥0.9), num_failed_logins≥1, and logged_in=0, e.g., guess_passwd attack samples
Signature 2: U2R attacks show root_shell=1, hot≥1, logged_in=1, and increased num_compromised and num_root counts, often with short duration and service ftp_data or telnet

Signature 3: Warezmaster and warezclient attacks characterized by src_bytes=0, very large dst_bytes (millions), flag=SF, and same_srv_rate=1.0 indicating repeated access to the same service with no data sent from source
technical_markers: root_shell=1 and num_root≥1 as markers of privilege escalation
rerror_rate and srv_rerror_rate ≥0.9 as indicators of connection rejection/failure in R2L attacks
hot≥1 combined with logged_in=1 and num_compromised≥1 in U2R attacks
dst_bytes > 5,000,000 with src_bytes=0 in warezmaster attacks
serror_rate and srv_serror_rate near zero in most attacks except some guess_passwd samples with serror_rate≈0.5
normal_indicators: Normal traffic predominantly uses protocol_type tcp, udp, and icmp with flag=SF
src_bytes and dst_bytes are balanced and moderate, with no extreme outliers
num_failed_logins=0 and logged_in=0 or 1 depending on session type
low or zero hot, num_compromised, root_shell, su_attempted, and num_root values
Stable connection patterns with high same_srv_rate (close to 1.0) and low error rates
baseline_metrics: serror_rate, srv_serror_rate, rerror_rate, srv_rerror_rate typically 0.0 in benign samples
count and srv_count can be high (e.g., 100+), reflecting normal repeated connections
dst_host_count and dst_host_srv_count often at maximum (255), indicating normal host activity
duration mostly 0 or low values, typical of normal short connections
hot=0 and num_failed_logins=0 in majority of benign samples
